subject: Clarify incident-notify timelines & subprocessor cooperation for FinBridge DPA
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@finbridge.com>; security@finbridge.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify incident-notify timelines & subprocessor cooperation for FinBridge DPA

Hi Sara / FinBridge team,

Thanks again for moving the DPA draft forward. A few items came up internally while we were reviewing Section 7 (Incident Notification & Cooperation) and I wanted to confirm expectations before we respond with redlines. High-level asks: 

- Timeline: you currently require "notification without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after discovery." We want to propose a two-step timeline that (a) requires initial acknowledgement/triage notification within 24 hours and (b) a substantive notice with scope and evidence cadence within 72 hours for incidents meeting the threshold. Can you confirm whether FinBridge will accept that structure?

- Subprocessors: how do you expect our subprocessors to be engaged for forensic evidence handoffs? We typically route requests through a designated liaison (security@redwood.com) and use a short-form data request + export token to preserve chain-of-custody. FinBridge mentions escrow/forensic transfer in Appendix B — is that intended to be a hard requirement or an option for high-severity incidents?

- Cross-border data: if evidence requires export from EU-hosted logs to a US forensic vendor, what consents or Data Transfer Agreement steps does FinBridge expect us to take in-scope? We can surface redacted telemetry or a forensics snapshot under standard SCCs, or leverage an EU-hosted partner.

I've attached our evidence-handoff checklist and a short security questionnaire that explains typical turnaround and redaction options. If it helps, we can hop on a 30-minute call to align (I can include Kimberly and Marissa).

Next step: we'd appreciate a short reply to the three bullets above so we can shape the redline.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
(Attachment: evidence_handoff_checklist.xlsx)
(Attachment: finbridge_scq_v2.pdf)

From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@finbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finbridge.com; procurement@finbridge.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify incident-notify timelines & subprocessor cooperation for FinBridge DPA

Ben — thanks for the clear questions, good to loop the security folks. A few quick answers from a FinBridge perspective: 

1) Timeline: we can be flexible on a two-step approach. Our concern is SLA for customer outreach — initial acknowledgement within 24 hours is acceptable. However, our legal team needs the "substantive notice" to include an incident severity classification and proposed customer notification cadence; 72 hours is OK for many incidents but we reserve the right to require a faster substantive disclosure for incidents affecting customer PII.

2) Subprocessors / evidence handoff: we prefer evidence transfer to be done via a named liaison and an encrypted artifact exchange (SFTP or secure shared container). Escrow is optional unless the incident involves immutable backups or long-term retention claims. We will accept a liaison flow as long as chain-of-custody metadata is preserved (timestamps, checksums, export manifests).

3) Cross-border: for EU-origin telemetry we expect minimal export (metadata + redacted logs) unless the parties agree a lawful basis. SCCs are fine; if you need an EU-hosted forensic vendor that’s also acceptable. Please note that in some regulated cases we will insist on in-region analysis.

Follow-up: I'm looping FinBridge Security (security@finbridge.com) and procurement — they may request a short form for escrow costs if needed. Happy to take a quick call; propose Fri 11/20 10am ET.

—Sara
Sara Khan | Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
FinBridge
(Attachment: none)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@finbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, security@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify incident-notify timelines & subprocessor cooperation for FinBridge DPA

Sara — perfect, appreciate the clarity. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- We'll propose the two-step timeline in our redline with the caveat you noted for PII-impacting incidents (we'll add language so Redwood will escalate classification within 12 hours of discovery to avoid delays).

- Evidence handoff: we'll keep escrow optional but add an "escrow triggers" list for when it becomes required (immutable backups, inability to produce original telemetry, or regulatory demand). We'll also include the liaison exchange format and manifest/checksum requirements so your security team can validate chain-of-custody.

- Cross-border: we'll offer an EU-hosted vendor option and SCC-backed transfers; we'll also propose an in-region-forensic clause where FinBridge may request in-region analysis for regulated data.

I've attached the SCQ and our evidence handoff checklist for your security team to review — includes the SFTP manifest spec and example timestamps. If the Fri 11/20 10am ET slot works, Kimberly will join to discuss operational runbooks and any procurement-level questions on escrow pricing.

Action items:
- Sara to confirm Fri 11/20 10am ET or propose alternate
- We will draft redline with the two-step timeline + escrow triggers + manifest fields by EOD Mon 11/23

Thanks — look forward to aligning.

Ben
